title: Module 2: Surveillance, Dark Patterns, and Learner Autonomy
description: Distinguish monitoring from surveillance, identify dark patterns specific to learner-facing AI (variable-ratio rewards, loss aversion, manufactured peer presence), and use self-determination theory to anchor a learner-autonomy-respecting design.
learning_objectives: State three properties (aggregation depth, asymmetry of access, inability to opt out) that distinguish surveillance from monitoring.
Recognize five dark patterns specific to learner-facing AI and the developmental concerns they exploit.
Apply self-determination theory's autonomy-competence-relatedness frame to evaluate an educational AI deployment.
Run a seven-step pre-deployment audit that combines legal floor, monitoring vs. surveillance, engagement mechanics, autonomy, and procedural due process.
